options.text: corrosion and it is a physical as well as chemical change

options.label: B
options.text: dissolution and it is a physical change

options.label: D

questions.canonical_answer_text: corrosion and it is a chemical change

questions.stem: Which of the following are physical changes? (i) Melting of iron metal (ii) Rusting of iron (iii) Bending of an iron rod (iv) Drawing a wire of iron metal
Which of the following are chemical changes? (i) Decaying of wood (ii) Burning of wood (iii) Sawing of wood (iv) Hammering of a nail into a piece of wood
What would you observe when a mixture of iron filings and sulphur powder is heated strongly?
questions.canonical_answer: A new substance, iron sulphide, is formed.
questions.canonical_answer_text: A new substance, iron sulphide, is formed.

questions.stem: Classify the following as physical or chemical properties: Zinc dissolves in hydrochloric acid with the evolution of hydrogen gas.
On heating calcium carbonate gets converted into calcium oxide and carbon dioxide. Is this a physical or a chemical change?
Name a non-metal which is required for combustion.

Iron filings and sulphur were mixed together and divided into two parts, ‘A’ and ‘B’. Part ‘A’ was heated strongly while Part ‘B’ was not heated. Dilute hydrochloric acid was added to both the Parts and evolution of gas was seen in both the cases. How will you identify the gases evolved?
questions.canonical_answer: Part A gives hydrogen sulphide; part B gives hydrogen. Hydrogen sulphide has a characteristic rotten-egg odour; hydrogen is identified by the pop test.
questions.canonical_answer_text: Part A gives hydrogen sulphide; part B gives hydrogen. Hydrogen sulphide has a characteristic rotten-egg odour; hydrogen is identified by the pop test.

questions.stem: Classify each of the following, as a physical or a chemical change. Give reasons. Burning of kerosene in a lantern.
questions.canonical_answer: Chemical change; new substances are formed during combustion.
questions.canonical_answer_text: Chemical change; new substances are formed during combustion.
